scope: Native MAP3 binary-construction error payload and 0..3 flatmap representation consumers. No MAP_EXT decoding, map instructions/BIFs, HAMT, exception flags/stacktraces, or bs_create_bin admission.
adaptations: Native flatmap_t prefix, MAP_HEADER_FLATMAP, separate keys tuple and contiguous values are preserved. The selected 0..3 size range is valid under both native Debug and Release policies; no HAMT or general map creation is admitted. MAP3 requires preordered unique keys; the error factory uses the native cause/function/module atom order.

Moving GC sizes map bodies from their size word, not generic header arity. It scans keys and values as roots, preserving sharing and offheap payload lifetimes. Flat sizing/copying and the private-append alias checker traverse those same roots. Unknown map headers/sizes abort rather than silently hiding children.

Native eq's flatmap branch compares sizes, then the keys tuple and values through the existing fallible term-array stack. OOM leaves equality output unchanged; no ordering, lookup/update or HAMT algorithm is inferred.

The complete operation-kind switch and MAP3/cause-tuple construction from erts_prepare_bs_construct_fail_info become a payload-only C factory. It does not assign freason/fvalue, encode EXF_HAS_EXT_INFO or implement stacktrace/catch behavior. BSC identities grant no execution permission.

A temporary owned process root protects the supplied value during the final fallible heap reservation, replacing HeapFragOnlyAlloc. Heap credit and old roots are preserved; output publication is last. Allocation failure is explicit and same-process retry is supported. Output slots cannot be pointers into a moving heap.

Native map-specific layouts/macros and BSC identities are separately compared using the already-oracled word/tuple primitives. Stock OTP supplies five actual binary-construction exception payload vectors; its fixture is never loaded into libbeam.

C-created error maps execute real identity and exact-comparison BEAM functions with moving collection; nested maps, scratch OOM, failed-copy reference rollback, writable aliases and copied binary survival across source-process destruction are tested. No new guest opcode, BIF, literal format or stateful acceptance is claimed.
